newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: India buys 870,000 tonnes of May diesel in tender.
newsitem.headline: India buys 870,000 tonnes of May diesel in tender.

text.p: State-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) has bought 870,000 tonnes of diesel by tender in 21 cargoes for deliveries in May, traders said on Monday.
Thirteen cargoes will be delivered to the Indian west coast ports, while eight cargoes will be delivered to the east coast.
Only two of the cargoes were for 0.5 percent sulphur diesel. The remaining cargoes were for 1.0-percent sulphur diesel cargoes.
West coast awards for 1.0-percent diesel were made between $23.30 and $26.75 per tonne premium to the high of Mediterranean quotes, cost and freight (c-and-f).
East coast cargoes for 1.0 percent diesel were awarded between $27.00 and $29.00 per tonne premium to the high of Mediterranean quotes, c-and-f.
East cargoes 0.5 percent sulphur were awarded around $28.00 per tonne premium and west coast around $27.00 per tonne premium.
But the traders also noted that the awards were made on a Mediterranean pricing basis, so sellers would want to cover their commitments as much as possible with cargoes from that region.
In the medium term, arbitrage cargoes of diesel from Russia and the Middle East, due to arrive in the second half of April and early May, could soften Asian price levels.
